raw.title: How to season cast iron
raw.author: Asha Rao
raw.text:
How to season cast iron
Seasoning is a thin layer of polymerised oil that protects cast iron from rust and gives the pan its non-stick surface. Apply a very thin coat of oil all over the pan and bake it upside down at 230 degrees Celsius for one hour.
Repeat the process three or four times when the pan is new. Avoid soaking the pan in water, and dry it on the stove after washing so no moisture is left in the pores of the metal.
When to re-season
If food starts to stick or the surface looks dull and grey, the seasoning has worn thin and the pan needs another round. Acidic sauces simmered for a long time are the usual cause.
